## 5.1 Secure Software Distribution and Delivery

[Read section 5.1 in the full text](/edi-stelsel-certification/text/nl-p-04w#s-5-1)

### INST-5.1-01 {#inst-5-1-01}

The Wallet Provider shall sign the Wallet Instance software package using a private key associated with the Wallet Provider’s registered identity in the target distribution platform’s certificate infrastructure, such that the distribution platform or device can verify the signature before permitting installation.

**Requirement** · obligation: **mandatory** · [PDF page 17](pathname:///files/edi-stelsel/2026-11-06/NL-P-04W_Wallet_Onboarding__Lifecycle_Mngt_-_reqs_-_RC1.0_-_for_pub.pdf#page=17)

**How a CAB verifies this:** A CAB verifies this requirement by reviewing the Wallet Provider’s code signing configuration and confirming that the signing key is registered with the Wallet Provider’s identity in the distribution platform. The CAB may also attempt to install a test package signed with an unregistered key and confirm that the target platform refuses installation.



### INST-5.1-02 {#inst-5-1-02}

The Wallet Provider shall distribute the Wallet Instance software exclusively through distribution channels that enforce signature verification of the software package as a condition of delivery to the Wallet User’s device.

**Requirement** · obligation: **mandatory** · [PDF page 17](pathname:///files/edi-stelsel/2026-11-06/NL-P-04W_Wallet_Onboarding__Lifecycle_Mngt_-_reqs_-_RC1.0_-_for_pub.pdf#page=17)

**How a CAB verifies this:** A CAB verifies this requirement by reviewing the Wallet Provider’s documented distribution channels and confirming that each channel enforces signature verification prior to delivery. The CAB examines whether any unapproved distribution paths exist and whether the Wallet Provider has controls to detect and respond to use of unauthorized channels.



### INST-5.1-03 {#inst-5-1-03}

The Wallet Provider shall ensure that the Wallet Instance verifies the integrity of its own software prior to initializing any Wallet Unit functionality, by performing a cryptographic check of the installed package against a reference value established at install time and protected within the device's hardware-backed key store or WSCD.

**Requirement** · obligation: **mandatory** · [PDF page 18](pathname:///files/edi-stelsel/2026-11-06/NL-P-04W_Wallet_Onboarding__Lifecycle_Mngt_-_reqs_-_RC1.0_-_for_pub.pdf#page=18)

**How a CAB verifies this:** A CAB verifies this requirement by reviewing the Wallet Provider's technical documentation and confirming that an integrity check is performed at each application launch prior to any Wallet Unit operation. The CAB may corroborate this by inspecting the launch-time integrity-check configuration and, where feasible, by testing that a modified application binary causes the Wallet Instance to refuse to initialise Wallet Unit functionality.



### INST-5.1-04 {#inst-5-1-04}

The Wallet Provider shall hold the private signing key used for the Wallet Instance software package in a hardware security module (HSM) that requires multi-person authorisation for each signing operation and that is certified to FIPS 140-3 Level 3, Common Criteria EAL4+, or an equivalent recognised level.

**Requirement** · obligation: **mandatory** · [PDF page 18](pathname:///files/edi-stelsel/2026-11-06/NL-P-04W_Wallet_Onboarding__Lifecycle_Mngt_-_reqs_-_RC1.0_-_for_pub.pdf#page=18)

**How a CAB verifies this:** A CAB verifies this requirement by reviewing the HSM certificate, the configured signing policy, and the access list for operators authorised to release a signature, and by sampling the audit log to confirm that recent signing events were performed under the multi-person policy.



### INST-5.1-05 {#inst-5-1-05}

The Wallet Provider shall record, in a tamper-evident log retained for at least 12 months, every administrative action that modifies the Wallet Instance software package, the code-signing infrastructure, or the configuration of the distribution channel, together with the identity of the operators and the time of the action.

**Requirement** · obligation: **mandatory** · [PDF page 19](pathname:///files/edi-stelsel/2026-11-06/NL-P-04W_Wallet_Onboarding__Lifecycle_Mngt_-_reqs_-_RC1.0_-_for_pub.pdf#page=19)

**How a CAB verifies this:** A CAB verifies this requirement by inspecting the log retention configuration and by sampling logs from the most recent 12 months for a selection of administrative event types to confirm they are retained and complete. The CAB may also review the tamper-evidence design and, where feasible, attempt under controlled conditions to alter a logged entry to confirm that tamper evidence is produced.



### INST-5.1-06 {#inst-5-1-06}

The Wallet Provider shall verify, before incorporating any third-party software component into a Wallet Instance software build, that the component's distribution origin is authenticated through a cryptographic signature or hash that traces to a publisher identity declared in the Wallet Provider's approved-supplier list.

**Requirement** · obligation: **mandatory** · [PDF page 19](pathname:///files/edi-stelsel/2026-11-06/NL-P-04W_Wallet_Onboarding__Lifecycle_Mngt_-_reqs_-_RC1.0_-_for_pub.pdf#page=19)

**How a CAB verifies this:** A CAB verifies this requirement by reviewing the approved-supplier list, the build configuration that enforces signature or hash verification, and the most recent SBOM produced by a build. Where feasible, the CAB may also attempt to introduce an



## 5.2 Device Security Pre-Checks

[Read section 5.2 in the full text](/edi-stelsel-certification/text/nl-p-04w#s-5-2)

### INST-5.2-01 {#inst-5-2-01}

The Wallet Provider shall ensure that the Wallet Instance, at installation and at each subsequent launch, verifies that the operating system version and security patch level of the host device meets the minimum requirements documented by the Wallet Provider, and refuses to activate Wallet Unit functionality on devices that do not meet those requirements.

**Requirement** · obligation: **mandatory** · [PDF page 20](pathname:///files/edi-stelsel/2026-11-06/NL-P-04W_Wallet_Onboarding__Lifecycle_Mngt_-_reqs_-_RC1.0_-_for_pub.pdf#page=20)

**How a CAB verifies this:** A CAB verifies this requirement by reviewing the Wallet Provider's documented minimum OS requirements and the implementation that enforces them, confirming that Wallet Unit functionality is not activated on a device that does not meet those requirements. Where feasible, the CAB may also test the Wallet Instance on such a device and confirm that the application refuses to activate Wallet Unit functionality.



### INST-5.2-02 {#inst-5-2-02}

The Wallet Provider shall ensure that the Wallet Instance detects the presence of root access or jailbreak conditions on the host device and, where such conditions are detected, refuses to finalize Wallet Instance Installation.

**Requirement** · obligation: **mandatory** · [PDF page 20](pathname:///files/edi-stelsel/2026-11-06/NL-P-04W_Wallet_Onboarding__Lifecycle_Mngt_-_reqs_-_RC1.0_-_for_pub.pdf#page=20)

**How a CAB verifies this:** A CAB verifies this requirement by reviewing the Wallet Provider's documented root/jailbreak-detection design and confirming that installation is refused on a rooted (Android) or jailbroken (iOS) device. Where feasible, the CAB may also attempt installation on a rooted or jailbroken test device to confirm that the Wallet Instance installation is impossible.



### INST-5.2-03 {#inst-5-2-03}

The Wallet Provider shall implement runtime anti-tampering controls in the Wallet Instance that detect attempts to instrument, hook, or modify the application's execution at runtime.

**Requirement** · obligation: **mandatory** · [PDF page 21](pathname:///files/edi-stelsel/2026-11-06/NL-P-04W_Wallet_Onboarding__Lifecycle_Mngt_-_reqs_-_RC1.0_-_for_pub.pdf#page=21)

**How a CAB verifies this:** A CAB verifies this requirement by reviewing the Wallet Provider's documented instrumentation-detection design and confirming that the application detects attachment of a dynamic instrumentation framework and refuses to process Wallet Unit operations. Where feasible, the CAB may also attach such a framework to a running test instance and confirm the detection and refusal.



### INST-5.2-04 {#inst-5-2-04}

The Wallet Provider shall ensure that the Wallet Unit refuses to finalize Wallet Instance installation when the runtime anti-tampering controls detect an attempt to instrument, hook, or modify the application's execution.

**Requirement** · obligation: **mandatory** · [PDF page 21](pathname:///files/edi-stelsel/2026-11-06/NL-P-04W_Wallet_Onboarding__Lifecycle_Mngt_-_reqs_-_RC1.0_-_for_pub.pdf#page=21)

**How a CAB verifies this:** A CAB verifies this requirement by reviewing the documented anti-tampering controls and confirming that installation performed under an instrumentation or hooking framework the controls detect does not finalise. Where feasible, the CAB may also run Wallet Instance installation under such a framework and confirm that installation does not finalise.



### INST-5.2-05 {#inst-5-2-05}

The Wallet Provider shall document and enforce minimum security requirements for devices on which the Wallet Instance may be installed and operated, including at minimum: a screen lock mechanism using a PIN, password, or biometric factor; the availability of a hardware-backed key store; and a supported operating system version receiving security updates from the platform vendor.

**Requirement** · obligation: **mandatory** · [PDF page 21](pathname:///files/edi-stelsel/2026-11-06/NL-P-04W_Wallet_Onboarding__Lifecycle_Mngt_-_reqs_-_RC1.0_-_for_pub.pdf#page=21)

**How a CAB verifies this:** A CAB verifies this requirement by reviewing the Wallet Provider's documented minimum device requirements and by confirming that the Wallet Instance refuses to activate Wallet Unit functionality on a test device that does not satisfy them.



### INST-5.2-06 {#inst-5-2-06}

The Wallet Provider shall ensure that the Wallet Secure Cryptographic Device used by the Wallet Unit is operated solely under the Wallet Provider’s control, holds a valid security certification appropriate for the applicable Assurance Level prior to its first use by a Wallet Unit, and remains under the Wallet Provider’s exclusive operational control throughout the entire lifetime of the Wallet Unit.

**Requirement** · obligation: **mandatory** · [PDF page 22](pathname:///files/edi-stelsel/2026-11-06/NL-P-04W_Wallet_Onboarding__Lifecycle_Mngt_-_reqs_-_RC1.0_-_for_pub.pdf#page=22)

**How a CAB verifies this:** A CAB verifies this requirement by reviewing the Wallet Provider’s documentation of the WSCD used in production, confirming that a valid security certification appropriate for the applicable Assurance Level is current and on record, and verifying that the Wallet Provider’s operational procedures ensure the WSCD remains under their exclusive control. The CAB also confirms that no pathway exists for parties other than the Wallet Provider to operate or access the WSCD.



### INST-5.2-07 {#inst-5-2-07}

The Wallet Provider shall implement mechanisms in the Wallet Instance to detect the presence of known malicious applications or anomalous runtime conditions on the host device that could expose Wallet Unit key material or credentials to unauthorised access, and shall, upon detection, prevent Wallet Unit operations involving access to key material until the threat is resolved.

**Requirement** · obligation: **mandatory** · [PDF page 23](pathname:///files/edi-stelsel/2026-11-06/NL-P-04W_Wallet_Onboarding__Lifecycle_Mngt_-_reqs_-_RC1.0_-_for_pub.pdf#page=23)

**How a CAB verifies this:** A CAB verifies this requirement by reviewing the Wallet Provider's threat detection implementation documentation and confirming that the Wallet Instance responds appropriately to a known malicious application signature or anomalous condition. Where feasible, the CAB may also test the Wallet Instance's behaviour when such a condition is simulated on the test device.



## 5.3 Installation Process Security

[Read section 5.3 in the full text](/edi-stelsel-certification/text/nl-p-04w#s-5-3)

### INST-5.3-01 {#inst-5-3-01}

The Wallet Provider shall distribute the Wallet Instance exclusively through the official app store of the operating system of the Wallet User's device; or, where distribution through alternative channels is necessary, shall implement a mechanism enabling even a Wallet User with low digital savviness to verify the authenticity of the Wallet Instance prior to installation and shall provide the Wallet User with clear instructions for completing that verification.

**Requirement** · obligation: **mandatory** · [PDF page 23](pathname:///files/edi-stelsel/2026-11-06/NL-P-04W_Wallet_Onboarding__Lifecycle_Mngt_-_reqs_-_RC1.0_-_for_pub.pdf#page=23)

**How a CAB verifies this:** A CAB verifies this requirement by confirming: (i) the primary distribution channel is the official OS app store, or (ii) the alternative distribution mechanism and the verification instructions are documented and validated during certification.



### INST-5.3-02 {#inst-5-3-02}

The Wallet Provider shall ensure that the Wallet Instance requests only those device permissions strictly necessary for the functioning of declared Wallet Unit features, and shall present the Wallet User with a plain-language explanation of the purpose of each permission at the time it is requested.

**Requirement** · obligation: **mandatory** · [PDF page 24](pathname:///files/edi-stelsel/2026-11-06/NL-P-04W_Wallet_Onboarding__Lifecycle_Mngt_-_reqs_-_RC1.0_-_for_pub.pdf#page=24)

**How a CAB verifies this:** A CAB verifies this requirement by reviewing the Wallet Provider's permission manifest and confirming that each declared permission is linked to a documented Wallet Unit feature, and by inspecting the installation flow to confirm that permission request screens include clear plain-language explanations. Where feasible, the CAB may also walk the installation flow on a test device to observe these explanations.



### INST-5.3-03 {#inst-5-3-03}

The Wallet Provider shall ensure that the Wallet Instance, at the time of installation, operates within an operating system-enforced isolation boundary that prevents co-located applications from accessing, reading, or modifying data stored by the Wallet Instance, including PID credentials, Electronic Attestations of Attributes, cryptographic key material, and any personal data processed by the Wallet Instance.

**Requirement** · obligation: **mandatory** · [PDF page 24](pathname:///files/edi-stelsel/2026-11-06/NL-P-04W_Wallet_Onboarding__Lifecycle_Mngt_-_reqs_-_RC1.0_-_for_pub.pdf#page=24)

**How a CAB verifies this:** A CAB verifies this requirement by reviewing the Wallet Provider's technical specification to confirm that the Wallet Instance relies on OS-enforced application sandboxing and that installation is refused on devices where sandboxing cannot be confirmed. Where feasible, the CAB may also attempt to read the Wallet Instance's private data storage from a co-located test application on a compliant device and confirm that access is denied by the OS.



### INST-5.3-04 {#inst-5-3-04}

The Wallet Provider shall ensure that the Wallet Instance is shipped with a secure default configuration such that no Wallet Unit functionality is accessible prior to completion of the initial activation process and no personal data is transmitted by the Wallet Instance before the Wallet User has accepted all required privacy disclosures.

**Requirement** · obligation: **mandatory** · [PDF page 25](pathname:///files/edi-stelsel/2026-11-06/NL-P-04W_Wallet_Onboarding__Lifecycle_Mngt_-_reqs_-_RC1.0_-_for_pub.pdf#page=25)

**How a CAB verifies this:** A CAB verifies this requirement by reviewing the documented pre-activation behaviour of the Wallet Instance and confirming that, before activation is complete, no Wallet Unit functionality is accessible, no sensitive data is transmitted, and the application does not accept connections from external services. Where feasible, the CAB may also test a freshly installed Wallet Instance prior to completing activation to confirm this behaviour.



## 5.4 Wallet User Information and Consent

[Read section 5.4 in the full text](/edi-stelsel-certification/text/nl-p-04w#s-5-4)

### INST-5.4-01 {#inst-5-4-01}

The Wallet Provider shall present the Wallet User, prior to completing installation of the Wallet Instance, with clear and comprehensible information about the nature of the wallet, the categories of personal data processed, the applicable terms and conditions, and the security responsibilities of the Wallet User.

**Requirement** · obligation: **mandatory** · [PDF page 25](pathname:///files/edi-stelsel/2026-11-06/NL-P-04W_Wallet_Onboarding__Lifecycle_Mngt_-_reqs_-_RC1.0_-_for_pub.pdf#page=25)

**How a CAB verifies this:** A CAB verifies this requirement by reviewing the Wallet Provider's documentation to confirm the content of the required disclosures - covering the categories of personal data, terms and conditions, and security responsibilities - and the mechanism for recording Wallet User consent. Where feasible, the CAB may also perform a fresh installation to confirm that all required disclosures are displayed before installation completes and that installation cannot proceed without acknowledgement of them.



### INST-5.4-02 {#inst-5-4-02}

The Wallet Provider shall ensure that the Wallet User is presented with the Wallet Provider's terms of service prior to completing installation of the Wallet Instance, that acceptance constitutes an explicit Wallet User action, and that the Wallet Instance is not operable until that acceptance has been recorded.

**Requirement** · obligation: **mandatory** · [PDF page 26](pathname:///files/edi-stelsel/2026-11-06/NL-P-04W_Wallet_Onboarding__Lifecycle_Mngt_-_reqs_-_RC1.0_-_for_pub.pdf#page=26)

**How a CAB verifies this:** A CAB verifies this requirement by reviewing the documented installation flow and confirming that the terms are presented before it completes, that acceptance requires an explicit Wallet User action, and that the Wallet Instance cannot be used if the acceptance step is bypassed. Where feasible, the CAB may also perform a fresh installation to confirm this behaviour.



### INST-5.4-03 {#inst-5-4-03}

The Wallet Provider shall ensure that, prior to completing installation of the Wallet Instance, the Wallet User is provided with a clear and complete description of all categories of personal data processed by the Wallet Unit, the purposes for which each category is processed, and the legal basis under Article 6 of the GDPR applicable to each processing activity.

**Requirement** · obligation: **mandatory** · [PDF page 26](pathname:///files/edi-stelsel/2026-11-06/NL-P-04W_Wallet_Onboarding__Lifecycle_Mngt_-_reqs_-_RC1.0_-_for_pub.pdf#page=26)

- **Legal references:** [GDPR](/edi-stelsel-certification/legal-basis#eu-2016-679)

**How a CAB verifies this:** A CAB verifies this requirement by reviewing the data processing disclosure presented during installation and confirming that: all processing activities are described; the purpose and legal basis for each is stated; and the disclosure is presented in plain language prior to completion of installation.



## 6.1 WSCD/WSCA Initialisation

[Read section 6.1 in the full text](/edi-stelsel-certification/text/nl-p-04w#s-6-1)

### ACT-6.1-01 {#act-6-1-01}

The Wallet Provider shall ensure that all communication between the Wallet Instance (WI) and the Wallet Secure Cryptographic Application (WSCA) during Wallet Unit activation is conducted over a channel that is mutually authenticated and integrity-protected, so that activation data cannot be intercepted, replayed, or tampered with by a third party.

**Requirement** · obligation: **mandatory** · [PDF page 28](pathname:///files/edi-stelsel/2026-11-06/NL-P-04W_Wallet_Onboarding__Lifecycle_Mngt_-_reqs_-_RC1.0_-_for_pub.pdf#page=28)

**How a CAB verifies this:** A CAB verifies this requirement by reviewing the technical specification of the WIWSCA interface and confirming that mutual authentication and integrity protection are documented and implemented for all supported WSCD architecture types.



### ACT-6.1-02 {#act-6-1-02}

The Wallet Provider shall ensure that all private keys attested in a Key Attestation and all private keys of device-bound PIDs and attestations are generated within the Wallet Secure Cryptographic Device (WSCD), and that those private keys are never extracted from the WSCD in the clear at any point during or after activation.

**Requirement** · obligation: **mandatory** · [PDF page 28](pathname:///files/edi-stelsel/2026-11-06/NL-P-04W_Wallet_Onboarding__Lifecycle_Mngt_-_reqs_-_RC1.0_-_for_pub.pdf#page=28)

**How a CAB verifies this:** A CAB verifies this requirement by reviewing the WSCD's certification documentation and confirming that key generation is an on-device operation and that no key extraction path exists in the clear.



### ACT-6.1-03 {#act-6-1-03}

The Wallet Provider shall verify, before signing and issuing a Key Attestation, that the public keys to be included in that Key Attestation correspond to private keys that were generated by and are stored in the WSCA/WSCD described in that attestation, and that those private keys remain under the exclusive control of the Wallet User.

**Requirement** · obligation: **mandatory** · [PDF page 28](pathname:///files/edi-stelsel/2026-11-06/NL-P-04W_Wallet_Onboarding__Lifecycle_Mngt_-_reqs_-_RC1.0_-_for_pub.pdf#page=28)

**How a CAB verifies this:** A CAB verifies this requirement by examining the key attestation mechanism documented in the Wallet Provider's technical specification and confirming that verification occurs prior to each WUA issuance.



## 6.2 Wallet Instance Attestation and Key Attestation Issuance

[Read section 6.2 in the full text](/edi-stelsel-certification/text/nl-p-04w#s-6-2)

### ACT-6.2-01 {#act-6-2-01}

The Wallet Provider shall, before issuing a Wallet Instance Attestation, verify that the requesting Wallet Instance is a genuine instance of its Wallet Solution and that the attestation request has not been replayed, forged, or submitted by an unauthorised party.

**Requirement** · obligation: **mandatory** · [PDF page 29](pathname:///files/edi-stelsel/2026-11-06/NL-P-04W_Wallet_Onboarding__Lifecycle_Mngt_-_reqs_-_RC1.0_-_for_pub.pdf#page=29)

**How a CAB verifies this:** A CAB verifies this requirement by reviewing the technical design of the WUA issuance protocol and confirming that both app authenticity verification and replay protection mechanisms are implemented and tested.



### ACT-6.2-02 {#act-6-2-02}

The Wallet Provider shall ensure that the Wallet Instance, during Wallet Unit activation, authenticates the Wallet Provider backend before transmitting any device or WSCD information, so that the Wallet Instance can verify it is communicating with the genuine Wallet Provider and not an impostor.

**Requirement** · obligation: **mandatory** · [PDF page 29](pathname:///files/edi-stelsel/2026-11-06/NL-P-04W_Wallet_Onboarding__Lifecycle_Mngt_-_reqs_-_RC1.0_-_for_pub.pdf#page=29)

**How a CAB verifies this:** A CAB verifies this requirement by reviewing the activation protocol specification and confirming that the Wallet Instance performs backend authentication prior to any transmission of device or WSCD data during activation.



### ACT-6.2-03 {#act-6-2-03}

The Wallet Provider shall ensure that each Key Attestation is cryptographically bound to the keystore of the Wallet Unit by including one or more public keys in the Key Attestation whose corresponding private keys are generated by and stored exclusively in the WSCA/WSCD of the Wallet Unit, so that each Key Attestation is tied to a specific, unique WSCD instance.

**Requirement** · obligation: **mandatory** · [PDF page 30](pathname:///files/edi-stelsel/2026-11-06/NL-P-04W_Wallet_Onboarding__Lifecycle_Mngt_-_reqs_-_RC1.0_-_for_pub.pdf#page=30)

**How a CAB verifies this:** A CAB verifies this requirement by examining the WUA issuance protocol and confirming that each WUA contains at least one public key with a corresponding private key provably stored in the described WSCA/WSCD.



### ACT-6.2-04 {#act-6-2-04}

The Wallet Provider shall ensure that each Key Attestation contains, at minimum: (a) information describing the storage type and the security certification of the WSCA/WSCD or keystore in which the attested private keys are stored; and (b) one or more public keys corresponding to private keys generated by and stored in that WSCA/WSCD or keystore.

**Requirement** · obligation: **mandatory** · [PDF page 30](pathname:///files/edi-stelsel/2026-11-06/NL-P-04W_Wallet_Onboarding__Lifecycle_Mngt_-_reqs_-_RC1.0_-_for_pub.pdf#page=30)

**How a CAB verifies this:** A CAB verifies this requirement by inspecting sample WUAs against the mandatory content list above and confirming compliance with the format specified in \[5\].



### ACT-6.2-05 {#act-6-2-05}

The Wallet Provider shall ensure that each Wallet Instance Attestation contains, at minimum: (a) information enabling PID Providers and Attestation Providers to check the revocation status of that Wallet Instance Attestation; and (b) a Wallet Unit identifier that does not enable tracking of the Wallet User across transactions.

**Requirement** · obligation: **mandatory** · [PDF page 30](pathname:///files/edi-stelsel/2026-11-06/NL-P-04W_Wallet_Onboarding__Lifecycle_Mngt_-_reqs_-_RC1.0_-_for_pub.pdf#page=30)

**How a CAB verifies this:** A CAB verifies this requirement by inspecting the content of Wallet Instance Attestations issued in production, by confirming that a revocation status reference is present and resolvable, and by confirming that the Wallet Unit identifier is not reused in a form that permits correlation between providers.



### ACT-6.2-06 {#act-6-2-06}

The Wallet Provider shall sign each Wallet Instance Attestation and each Key Attestation using only cryptographic algorithms included in the ECCG Agreed Cryptographic Mechanisms \[6\].

**Requirement** · obligation: **mandatory** · [PDF page 31](pathname:///files/edi-stelsel/2026-11-06/NL-P-04W_Wallet_Onboarding__Lifecycle_Mngt_-_reqs_-_RC1.0_-_for_pub.pdf#page=31)

**How a CAB verifies this:** A CAB verifies this requirement by reviewing the cryptographic algorithm selection documented in the Wallet Provider's security specification and confirming that contextbinding is implemented for all WUA presentations.



### ACT-6.2-07 {#act-6-2-07}

The Wallet Provider shall bind each Key Attestation to the specific issuance context in which it is presented, either by incorporating a nonce provided by the PID Provider or Attestation Provider into the Key Attestation, or by presenting the Key Attestation together with a Proof-of-Possession signed over that nonce using a private key attested in that Key Attestation.

**Requirement** · obligation: **mandatory** · [PDF page 31](pathname:///files/edi-stelsel/2026-11-06/NL-P-04W_Wallet_Onboarding__Lifecycle_Mngt_-_reqs_-_RC1.0_-_for_pub.pdf#page=31)

**How a CAB verifies this:** A CAB verifies this requirement by reviewing the WUA issuance protocol design and confirming that a Key Attestation presented in an exchange other than the one it was



### ACT-6.2-08 {#act-6-2-08}

The Wallet Provider shall ensure that all unique elements of each Wallet Instance Attestation and each Key Attestation — including the attestation identifier used for revocation status checking, the attested public keys, and the Wallet Provider's signature — have a negligible probability of having the same value across all such attestations issued by that Wallet Provider.

**Requirement** · obligation: **mandatory** · [PDF page 32](pathname:///files/edi-stelsel/2026-11-06/NL-P-04W_Wallet_Onboarding__Lifecycle_Mngt_-_reqs_-_RC1.0_-_for_pub.pdf#page=32)

**How a CAB verifies this:** A CAB verifies this requirement by reviewing the WUA generation implementation and confirming that CSPRNGs are used for all unique elements.



### ACT-6.2-09 {#act-6-2-09}

The Wallet Provider shall manage the validity periods of Wallet Instance Attestations and Key Attestations such that a non-revoked Wallet Unit can at all times present a Wallet Instance Attestation and a Key Attestation each with a remaining validity period of at least 31 days, and shall set validity periods taking into account the risk that such an attestation could become a vector for tracking the Wallet User across multiple issuance transactions.

**Requirement** · obligation: **mandatory** · [PDF page 32](pathname:///files/edi-stelsel/2026-11-06/NL-P-04W_Wallet_Onboarding__Lifecycle_Mngt_-_reqs_-_RC1.0_-_for_pub.pdf#page=32)

**How a CAB verifies this:** A CAB verifies this requirement by reviewing the WUA validity period policy and confirming that renewal processes are tested to ensure uninterrupted WUA availability.



### ACT-6.2-10 {#act-6-2-10}

The Wallet Provider shall re-issue Wallet Instance Attestations and Key Attestations to a non-revoked Wallet Unit as needed throughout the lifetime of the Wallet Unit, ensuring continuity of the Wallet Unit's ability to receive PIDs and device-bound attestations without requiring re-activation.

**Requirement** · obligation: **mandatory** · [PDF page 32](pathname:///files/edi-stelsel/2026-11-06/NL-P-04W_Wallet_Onboarding__Lifecycle_Mngt_-_reqs_-_RC1.0_-_for_pub.pdf#page=32)

**How a CAB verifies this:** A CAB verifies this requirement by confirming that the WUA renewal workflow is documented and tested, and that no degradation in security verification occurs during renewal compared to initial activation.



### ACT-6.2-11 {#act-6-2-11}

The Wallet Provider shall ensure that device binding for all PIDs and devicebound attestations is implemented by having the WSCA/WSCD or keystore generate a dedicated public-private key pair for each PID or device-bound attestation, and by ensuring that the corresponding private key is generated within and remains protected by the WSCA/WSCD or keystore throughout the lifetime of the attestation.

**Requirement** · obligation: **mandatory** · [PDF page 33](pathname:///files/edi-stelsel/2026-11-06/NL-P-04W_Wallet_Onboarding__Lifecycle_Mngt_-_reqs_-_RC1.0_-_for_pub.pdf#page=33)

**How a CAB verifies this:** A CAB verifies this requirement by reviewing the issuance protocol documentation for each attestation type and confirming that a new key pair is generated per issuance, by requesting sample issuance transactions and verifying that the public keys differ, and by confirming that the Wallet Provider's WSCA/WSCD architecture prevents key pair reuse across attestation instances.



### ACT-6.2-12 {#act-6-2-12}

The Wallet Provider shall ensure that every public key to which a PID or a device-bound attestation is bound at issuance is a public key attested in a Key Attestation issued to that Wallet Unit.

**Requirement** · obligation: **mandatory** · [PDF page 33](pathname:///files/edi-stelsel/2026-11-06/NL-P-04W_Wallet_Onboarding__Lifecycle_Mngt_-_reqs_-_RC1.0_-_for_pub.pdf#page=33)

**How a CAB verifies this:** A CAB verifies this requirement by comparing, for a sample of issuances, the public key in the issued credential against the set of public keys attested in the Key Attestation presented during that issuance, and by reviewing the issuance logic that enforces this correspondence. Where feasible, the CAB may also attempt an issuance with a key that is absent from the Key Attestation to confirm that it is refused.



### ACT-6.2-13 {#act-6-2-13}

The Wallet Provider shall establish and maintain a documented policy governing the issuance of Wallet Instance Attestations and Key Attestations that satisfies the requirements of clauses 6 and 7 of \[9\].

**Requirement** · obligation: **mandatory** · [PDF page 34](pathname:///files/edi-stelsel/2026-11-06/NL-P-04W_Wallet_Onboarding__Lifecycle_Mngt_-_reqs_-_RC1.0_-_for_pub.pdf#page=34)

**How a CAB verifies this:** A CAB verifies this requirement by reviewing the attestation issuance policy against clauses 6 and 7 of \[9\] and by confirming that the version in force corresponds to the practices observed during the assessment.



### ACT-6.2-14 {#act-6-2-14}

The Wallet Provider shall ensure that the revocation-status-maintenance period of each Wallet Instance Attestation and each Key Attestation it issues to a Wallet Unit is at least as long as the longest administrative validity period of any PID or device-bound Electronic Attestation of Attributes issued into that Wallet Unit on the basis of that Wallet Instance Attestation or Key Attestation, and that the revocation status is maintained throughout that period.

**Requirement** · obligation: **mandatory** · [PDF page 34](pathname:///files/edi-stelsel/2026-11-06/NL-P-04W_Wallet_Onboarding__Lifecycle_Mngt_-_reqs_-_RC1.0_-_for_pub.pdf#page=34)

**How a CAB verifies this:** A CAB verifies this requirement by reviewing the Wallet Provider's documented policy for setting the revocation-status-maintenance period of Wallet Instance Attestations and Key Attestations and confirming that it is at least as long as the longest administrative validity period of the PIDs and device-bound Electronic Attestations of Attributes issued into the Wallet Unit, and by inspecting issuance records to confirm the committed periods. Where feasible, the CAB may issue a device-bound credential with a long administrative validity and confirm that the maintenance period committed in the corresponding Wallet Instance Attestation and Key Attestation is at least as long.



## 6.3 Wallet Instance – Wallet Unit Binding

[Read section 6.3 in the full text](/edi-stelsel-certification/text/nl-p-04w#s-6-3)

### ACT-6.3-01 {#act-6-3-01}

The Wallet Provider shall establish the binding between the Wallet Instance and the Wallet Unit by issuing a Wallet Unit Attestation only to a Wallet Instance whose installation has been successfully verified through a platform-level attestation mechanism provided by the device operating system.

**Requirement** · obligation: **mandatory** · [PDF page 35](pathname:///files/edi-stelsel/2026-11-06/NL-P-04W_Wallet_Onboarding__Lifecycle_Mngt_-_reqs_-_RC1.0_-_for_pub.pdf#page=35)

**How a CAB verifies this:** A CAB verifies this requirement by reviewing the WUA issuance protocol specification and confirming that a platform attestation step is performed before any WUA is issued. Where feasible, the CAB may also test whether the activation process rejects a modified Wallet Instance or one running on an environment that does not produce a valid platform attestation.



### ACT-6.3-02 {#act-6-3-02}

The Wallet Provider shall not use persistent device fingerprinting for fraud monitoring or risk assessment purposes; where device-specific identifiers are collected during activation for legitimate operational purposes, the Wallet Provider shall limit collection to the minimum necessary, shall not derive or retain a persistent fingerprint for Wallet User tracking, and shall inform the Wallet User in accordance with the requirements of the General Data Protection Regulation.

**Requirement** · obligation: **mandatory** · [PDF page 35](pathname:///files/edi-stelsel/2026-11-06/NL-P-04W_Wallet_Onboarding__Lifecycle_Mngt_-_reqs_-_RC1.0_-_for_pub.pdf#page=35)

**How a CAB verifies this:** A CAB verifies this requirement by reviewing the data processing inventory of the Wallet Provider and confirming that no persistent device fingerprinting mechanism is implemented for fraud or risk monitoring.



### ACT-6.3-03 {#act-6-3-03}

The Wallet Provider shall ensure that each Wallet Instance holds cryptographic material that can be used to identify unambiguously the Wallet Instance in a way that this cryptographic data cannot be cloned to another device.

**Requirement** · obligation: **mandatory** · [PDF page 36](pathname:///files/edi-stelsel/2026-11-06/NL-P-04W_Wallet_Onboarding__Lifecycle_Mngt_-_reqs_-_RC1.0_-_for_pub.pdf#page=36)

**How a CAB verifies this:** A CAB verifies this requirement by reviewing the Wallet Provider's technical architecture for the Wallet Instance cryptographic material and confirming in the design documentation that the material is generated and stored protected at the level specified in the risk analysis. Where feasible, the CAB may also test that the Wallet Instance cannot be successfully authenticated from a device that lacks the required protection or from a copy of the application data restored to a different device.



### ACT-6.3-04 {#act-6-3-04}

The Wallet Provider shall ensure that the WSCA authenticates the Wallet Instance before performing any cryptographic operation on its behalf, by challenging the Wallet Instance to produce a proof of possession of the cryptographic data mentioned in ACT-5.3-03.

**Requirement** · obligation: **mandatory** · [PDF page 36](pathname:///files/edi-stelsel/2026-11-06/NL-P-04W_Wallet_Onboarding__Lifecycle_Mngt_-_reqs_-_RC1.0_-_for_pub.pdf#page=36)

**How a CAB verifies this:** A CAB verifies this requirement by reviewing the WSCA-to-Wallet-Instance interface protocol specification and confirming that a challenge-response step is performed before each WSCA operation. Where feasible, the CAB may also test that the WSCA rejects requests accompanied by an invalid or absent identity signature.



## 6.4 Wallet User Account Setup with Wallet Provider

[Read section 6.4 in the full text](/edi-stelsel-certification/text/nl-p-04w#s-6-4)

### ACT-6.4-01 {#act-6-4-01}

The Wallet Provider shall offer the Wallet User the opportunity to authenticate to an existing Wallet User account before offering the creation of a new Wallet User account during Wallet Unit activation.

**Requirement** · obligation: **mandatory** · [PDF page 37](pathname:///files/edi-stelsel/2026-11-06/NL-P-04W_Wallet_Onboarding__Lifecycle_Mngt_-_reqs_-_RC1.0_-_for_pub.pdf#page=37)

**How a CAB verifies this:** A CAB verifies this requirement by reviewing the documented activation flow for a Wallet User who already holds an account and confirming that authentication to the existing account is offered before the option to create a new account. Where feasible, the CAB may also walk the activation flow on a test device to confirm this ordering.



### ACT-6.4-02 {#act-6-4-02}

The Wallet Provider shall not collect or process personal identity data about the Wallet User during Wallet Unit activation beyond what is strictly necessary to complete the activation process and to comply with applicable legal obligations.

**Requirement** · obligation: **mandatory** · [PDF page 37](pathname:///files/edi-stelsel/2026-11-06/NL-P-04W_Wallet_Onboarding__Lifecycle_Mngt_-_reqs_-_RC1.0_-_for_pub.pdf#page=37)

**How a CAB verifies this:** A CAB verifies this requirement by reviewing the Wallet Provider's activation data processing inventory and confirming that each data element has a documented necessity and legal basis. Where feasible, the CAB may also test the activation flow to confirm that no personal identity data beyond the documented minimum is requested or stored.



### ACT-6.4-03 {#act-6-4-03}

The Wallet Provider shall ensure that any modification to the Wallet Unit account configuration after activation requires authenticated and authorised proof from the Wallet Unit or, for emergency procedures, a fresh verification of the Wallet User's identity, and cannot be performed unilaterally by the Wallet Provider without the Wallet User's involvement.

**Requirement** · obligation: **mandatory** · [PDF page 38](pathname:///files/edi-stelsel/2026-11-06/NL-P-04W_Wallet_Onboarding__Lifecycle_Mngt_-_reqs_-_RC1.0_-_for_pub.pdf#page=38)

**How a CAB verifies this:** A CAB verifies this requirement by reviewing the account management procedures and confirming that modification requests submitted to the Wallet Provider backend without a valid Wallet Unit proof of possession are rejected and that the emergency recovery procedure requires documented identity re-verification. Where feasible, the CAB may also test that such a modification request without valid proof of possession is rejected.



### ACT-6.4-04 {#act-6-4-04}

The Wallet Provider shall present the Wallet User with configurable privacy settings during activation, and shall ensure that the default configuration of any optional data processing activity is set to the option that minimises data collection unless the Wallet User has explicitly selected otherwise.

**Requirement** · obligation: **mandatory** · [PDF page 38](pathname:///files/edi-stelsel/2026-11-06/NL-P-04W_Wallet_Onboarding__Lifecycle_Mngt_-_reqs_-_RC1.0_-_for_pub.pdf#page=38)

**How a CAB verifies this:** A CAB verifies this requirement by reviewing the activation Wallet User interface flow and confirming that optional data processing settings are presented and default to the most privacy-protective option, and that the post-activation settings interface allows the Wallet User to view and change privacy choices. Where feasible, the CAB may also exercise the settings interface on a test device to confirm this.



### ACT-6.4-05 {#act-6-4-05}

The Wallet Provider shall establish and maintain a Wallet User account mechanism that enables the Wallet User to request revocation of the Wallet Unit independently of physical access to the device on which the Wallet Instance is installed.

**Requirement** · obligation: **mandatory** · [PDF page 39](pathname:///files/edi-stelsel/2026-11-06/NL-P-04W_Wallet_Onboarding__Lifecycle_Mngt_-_reqs_-_RC1.0_-_for_pub.pdf#page=39)

**How a CAB verifies this:** A CAB verifies this requirement by reviewing the Wallet Provider's documentation for a Wallet User account facility that enables device-independent revocation and confirming that the account is established during the activation flow rather than on first use after a loss event. Where feasible, the CAB may also test that the revocation mechanism can be successfully invoked from a device other than the one hosting the Wallet Instance.



### ACT-6.4-06 {#act-6-4-06}

The Wallet Provider shall design the Wallet User account for revocation such that the revocation mechanism is accessible to the Wallet User under adverse conditions — including loss of the device, physical displacement, limited access to communications, or a state of stress — while being sufficiently protected against unauthorised use to prevent a third party from revoking the Wallet Unit of another person without that person's authorisation.

**Requirement** · obligation: **mandatory** · [PDF page 39](pathname:///files/edi-stelsel/2026-11-06/NL-P-04W_Wallet_Onboarding__Lifecycle_Mngt_-_reqs_-_RC1.0_-_for_pub.pdf#page=39)

**How a CAB verifies this:** A CAB verifies this requirement by reviewing the Wallet Provider's threat model and design documentation to confirm that the revocation mechanism has been assessed against multiple adverse-condition scenarios, and that the documented design guidelines explicitly acknowledge the risk asymmetry between inaccessibility and unauthorised revocation.



## 6.5 Wallet User Authentication Setup

[Read section 6.5 in the full text](/edi-stelsel-certification/text/nl-p-04w#s-6-5)

### ACT-6.5-01 {#act-6-5-01}

The Wallet Provider shall ensure that all authentication verification data associated with authentication factors enrolled during activation is stored either within the WSCA/WSCD or in platform-provided hardware-backed key storage, and is not accessible to any application other than the Wallet Instance.

**Requirement** · obligation: **mandatory** · [PDF page 40](pathname:///files/edi-stelsel/2026-11-06/NL-P-04W_Wallet_Onboarding__Lifecycle_Mngt_-_reqs_-_RC1.0_-_for_pub.pdf#page=40)

**How a CAB verifies this:** A CAB verifies this requirement by reviewing the design documentation for authentication credential storage and confirming that the storage location is hardware-



### ACT-6.5-02 {#act-6-5-02}

The Wallet Provider shall ensure that each authentication factor enrolled during Wallet Unit activation is cryptographically bound to that specific Wallet Unit, such that the same factor presented from any other device, copy, or instance cannot authenticate the holder for actions performed by the Wallet Unit.

**Requirement** · obligation: **mandatory** · [PDF page 41](pathname:///files/edi-stelsel/2026-11-06/NL-P-04W_Wallet_Onboarding__Lifecycle_Mngt_-_reqs_-_RC1.0_-_for_pub.pdf#page=41)

**How a CAB verifies this:** A CAB verifies this requirement by reviewing the design documentation of the Wallet Unit's authentication subsystem and inspecting how factor verification material is stored and protected, confirming that a clone cannot authenticate as the original holder. Where feasible, the CAB may also attempt to perform authentication on a clone of an enrolled Wallet Unit on a separate device using captured factor presentation data and confirm that the clone cannot authenticate.



### ACT-6.5-03 {#act-6-5-03}

The Wallet Provider shall ensure that the Wallet Unit limits the number of consecutive unsuccessful authentication attempts for each knowledge-based factor to a value not exceeding ten, beyond which the factor is locked until the Wallet User re-establishes proof of holder identity through an out-of-band procedure operated by the Wallet Provider.

**Requirement** · obligation: **mandatory** · [PDF page 41](pathname:///files/edi-stelsel/2026-11-06/NL-P-04W_Wallet_Onboarding__Lifecycle_Mngt_-_reqs_-_RC1.0_-_for_pub.pdf#page=41)

**How a CAB verifies this:** A CAB verifies this requirement by reviewing the Wallet Unit's design documentation for the attempt counter and the documented out-of-band unlock procedure, confirming



### ACT-6.5-04 {#act-6-5-04}

The Wallet Provider shall ensure that the Wallet User authentication mechanism established during Wallet Unit activation consists of at least two factors of different categories, each verified by the Wallet Secure Cryptographic Application of the Wallet Unit, such that no Wallet Unit operation involving Person Identification Data, the Wallet Unit Attestation, or other attestations at security level High can complete based solely on the Wallet User-device operating-system authentication mechanism.

**Requirement** · obligation: **mandatory** · [PDF page 42](pathname:///files/edi-stelsel/2026-11-06/NL-P-04W_Wallet_Onboarding__Lifecycle_Mngt_-_reqs_-_RC1.0_-_for_pub.pdf#page=42)

**How a CAB verifies this:** A CAB verifies this requirement by reviewing the design documentation for the authentication subsystem and confirming that for PID, WUA, and security-level-High attestation operations the WSCA performs verification of the Wallet User factor itself rather than relying on the OS authentication result alone. Where feasible, the CAB may also attempt on a test Wallet Unit to perform such an operation while supplying only an OS-level authentication and confirm that the operation is rejected.



## 6.6 Migration Object import

[Read section 6.6 in the full text](/edi-stelsel-certification/text/nl-p-04w#s-6-6)

### ACT-6.6-01 {#act-6-6-01}

The Wallet Provider shall present the Wallet User with the option to restore a Migration Object from another Wallet Unit from the Wallet User.

**Requirement** · obligation: **mandatory** · [PDF page 42](pathname:///files/edi-stelsel/2026-11-06/NL-P-04W_Wallet_Onboarding__Lifecycle_Mngt_-_reqs_-_RC1.0_-_for_pub.pdf#page=42)

**How a CAB verifies this:** A CAB verifies this requirement by reviewing the documented activation flow and confirming that the Wallet User is offered the option to restore from a Migration Object before the Wallet Unit is activated empty. Where feasible, the CAB may also run the activation flow on a test device to confirm the option is offered.



### ACT-6.6-02 {#act-6-6-02}

When the Wallet User provides a Migration Object, the Wallet Unit shall, upon receiving the decryption password from the Wallet User, import all data from the Migration Object.

**Requirement** · obligation: **mandatory** · [PDF page 43](pathname:///files/edi-stelsel/2026-11-06/NL-P-04W_Wallet_Onboarding__Lifecycle_Mngt_-_reqs_-_RC1.0_-_for_pub.pdf#page=43)

**How a CAB verifies this:** A CAB verifies this requirement by reviewing the documented import procedure and confirming that the correct password is required for a Migration Object to be imported. Where feasible, the CAB may also attempt an import without the password to confirm it fails, then supply the correct password and confirm the data is imported.



### ACT-6.6-03 {#act-6-6-03}

After import of the data from a Migration Object, the Wallet Unit shall offer to guide the Wallet User through the re-issuance of the key bound PID and attestations, allowing the Wallet User to select which PID and EAA to have re-issued at that moment.

**Requirement** · obligation: **mandatory** · [PDF page 43](pathname:///files/edi-stelsel/2026-11-06/NL-P-04W_Wallet_Onboarding__Lifecycle_Mngt_-_reqs_-_RC1.0_-_for_pub.pdf#page=43)

**How a CAB verifies this:** A CAB verifies this requirement by reviewing the documented restore procedure and confirming that the Wallet Unit guides the Wallet User through re-issuance and allows a subset of credentials to be selected. Where feasible, the CAB may also import a Migration Object on a test device to confirm this behaviour.



### ACT-6.6-04 {#act-6-6-04}

If the Wallet User has not chosen to re-issue all PID and EAA in one go, the Wallet User should have the opportunity to restart the process at a later stage.

**Requirement** · obligation: **mandatory** · [PDF page 43](pathname:///files/edi-stelsel/2026-11-06/NL-P-04W_Wallet_Onboarding__Lifecycle_Mngt_-_reqs_-_RC1.0_-_for_pub.pdf#page=43)

**How a CAB verifies this:** A CAB verifies this requirement by reviewing the documented restore procedure and confirming that, when only part of the credential set is re-issued, the Wallet Unit offers a way to re-issue the remaining credentials in a later session. Where feasible, the CAB may also re-issue only part of the credential set during a restore and confirm the remaining credentials can be re-issued later.



### ACT-6.6-05 — The Wallet Unit shall support all restore mechanisms specified in \[7\]. {#act-6-6-05}

The Wallet Unit shall support all restore mechanisms specified in \[7\].

**Requirement** · obligation: **mandatory** · [PDF page 44](pathname:///files/edi-stelsel/2026-11-06/NL-P-04W_Wallet_Onboarding__Lifecycle_Mngt_-_reqs_-_RC1.0_-_for_pub.pdf#page=44)

**How a CAB verifies this:** A CAB verifies this requirement by reviewing the documented set of supported Migration Object mechanisms and confirming that the Wallet Unit imports an object produced by each. Where feasible, the CAB may also restore Migration Objects produced by each supported mechanism and confirm that the Wallet Unit imports each correctly.



## 6.7 Migration Object Setup

[Read section 6.7 in the full text](/edi-stelsel-certification/text/nl-p-04w#s-6-7)

### ACT-6.7-01 {#act-6-7-01}

The Wallet Provider shall present the Wallet User with an explicit choice about whether to create a Migration Object during the Wallet Unit activation process, before the activation process is considered complete.

**Requirement** · obligation: **mandatory** · [PDF page 44](pathname:///files/edi-stelsel/2026-11-06/NL-P-04W_Wallet_Onboarding__Lifecycle_Mngt_-_reqs_-_RC1.0_-_for_pub.pdf#page=44)

**How a CAB verifies this:** A CAB verifies this requirement by reviewing the documented activation flow and confirming that: (i) a dedicated Migration Object choice screen is present; (ii) neither



### ACT-6.7-02 {#act-6-7-02}

When presenting the Migration Object choice, the Wallet Provider shall inform the Wallet User in plain language that without a Migration Object: (a) there will be no list of PID and Wallet Bound EAA for the new Wallet Unit to request reissuance; (b) the transaction log will not be preserved, and the Wallet User will have no means to demonstrate past transactions in the event of a dispute, fraud, or security incident; (c) there will be no mechanism for migrating the non Wallet Bound EAA to a new Wallet Unit.

**Requirement** · obligation: **mandatory** · [PDF page 45](pathname:///files/edi-stelsel/2026-11-06/NL-P-04W_Wallet_Onboarding__Lifecycle_Mngt_-_reqs_-_RC1.0_-_for_pub.pdf#page=45)

**How a CAB verifies this:** A CAB verifies this requirement by reviewing the Migration Object choice screen text and confirming that all three consequence items are explicitly and separately stated in Wallet User-facing language. In localised implementations, each language version is assessed for completeness of all three items.



### ACT-6.7-03 {#act-6-7-03}

The Wallet Provider shall not complete Wallet Unit activation until the Wallet User has explicitly confirmed their choice regarding the Migration Object.

**Requirement** · obligation: **mandatory** · [PDF page 45](pathname:///files/edi-stelsel/2026-11-06/NL-P-04W_Wallet_Onboarding__Lifecycle_Mngt_-_reqs_-_RC1.0_-_for_pub.pdf#page=45)

**How a CAB verifies this:** A CAB verifies this requirement by reviewing the activation flow and confirming that: (i) a distinct Migration Object choice screen is present; (ii) the disclosure covers all three items of ACT-5.7-02; (iii) the activation process cannot be completed without a distinct confirmation action by the Wallet User; (iv) the confirmation is recorded in the activation log.



### ACT-6.7-04 {#act-6-7-04}

\[CONDITIONAL\] Where the Wallet User chooses to create a Migration Object during activation, the Wallet Unit shall require the Wallet User to designate a storage location for the Migration Object before the activation process is considered complete.

**Requirement** · obligation: **conditional** · [PDF page 46](pathname:///files/edi-stelsel/2026-11-06/NL-P-04W_Wallet_Onboarding__Lifecycle_Mngt_-_reqs_-_RC1.0_-_for_pub.pdf#page=46)

**How a CAB verifies this:** A CAB verifies this requirement by confirming that: (i) when the Wallet User selects the option to create a Migration Object, a storage location selection step is present in the activation flow; (ii) activation cannot complete without a storage location being confirmed; (iii) the designated storage location is recorded in the Wallet Unit's activation record.



### ACT-6.7-05 {#act-6-7-05}

The Wallet Provider shall ensure that at least one storage option offered for the Migration Object is EU based and under the Wallet User’s exclusive control and is not a location controlled by the Wallet Provider.

**Requirement** · obligation: **mandatory** · [PDF page 46](pathname:///files/edi-stelsel/2026-11-06/NL-P-04W_Wallet_Onboarding__Lifecycle_Mngt_-_reqs_-_RC1.0_-_for_pub.pdf#page=46)



### ACT-6.7-06 — The Wallet Unit shall create the Migration Object in accordance with \[7\]. {#act-6-7-06}

The Wallet Unit shall create the Migration Object in accordance with \[7\].

**Requirement** · obligation: **mandatory** · [PDF page 47](pathname:///files/edi-stelsel/2026-11-06/NL-P-04W_Wallet_Onboarding__Lifecycle_Mngt_-_reqs_-_RC1.0_-_for_pub.pdf#page=47)

**How a CAB verifies this:** A CAB verifies this requirement by creating a Migration Object on a test Wallet Unit and confirming that its structure and protection conform and that it imports successfully on a second Wallet Unit.



## 7.1 Security Requirements for Non-PID Use Cases

[Read section 7.1 in the full text](/edi-stelsel-certification/text/nl-p-04w#s-7-1)

### OPS-7.1-01 {#ops-7-1-01}

The Wallet Provider shall ensure that non-identity attestations stored in the Wallet Unit are protected against unauthorised access or modification by mechanisms equivalent to those applied to PID credentials stored in the same Wallet Unit.

**Requirement** · obligation: **mandatory** · [PDF page 48](pathname:///files/edi-stelsel/2026-11-06/NL-P-04W_Wallet_Onboarding__Lifecycle_Mngt_-_reqs_-_RC1.0_-_for_pub.pdf#page=48)

**How a CAB verifies this:** A CAB verifies this requirement by reviewing the storage and access-control design and confirming that non-identity attestations are held under the same protections as PID credentials and that access to them requires the same controls. Where feasible, the CAB may also test that access to non-identity attestations requires the same controls.



### OPS-7.1-02 {#ops-7-1-02}

The Wallet Provider shall ensure that the Wallet Unit discloses data from nonidentity attestations only in response to a verified relying party request and only to the minimum extent necessary to fulfil that request.

**Requirement** · obligation: **mandatory** · [PDF page 48](pathname:///files/edi-stelsel/2026-11-06/NL-P-04W_Wallet_Onboarding__Lifecycle_Mngt_-_reqs_-_RC1.0_-_for_pub.pdf#page=48)

**How a CAB verifies this:** A CAB verifies this requirement by issuing presentation requests from verified and unverified test relying parties and confirming that disclosure occurs only for the verified party and is limited to the requested elements.



### OPS-7.1-03 {#ops-7-1-03}

The Wallet Provider shall ensure that the Wallet Unit in the operational state without PID does not complete presentations of credentials or attestations whose issuance or validity depends on a PID credential bound to that Wallet Unit.

**Requirement** · obligation: **mandatory** · [PDF page 48](pathname:///files/edi-stelsel/2026-11-06/NL-P-04W_Wallet_Onboarding__Lifecycle_Mngt_-_reqs_-_RC1.0_-_for_pub.pdf#page=48)

**How a CAB verifies this:** A CAB verifies this requirement by reviewing the design of the operational state and confirming that a Wallet Unit without PID refuses to present attestations whose issuance requires PID binding and does not allow the relying party interaction to proceed to the presentation of PID-dependent credentials. Where feasible, the CAB may also deploy a Wallet Unit in the operational state without PID and attempt such a presentation to confirm it is refused.



## 7.2 Preparedness for PID Issuance

[Read section 7.2 in the full text](/edi-stelsel-certification/text/nl-p-04w#s-7-2)

### OPS-7.2-01 {#ops-7-2-01}

The Wallet Provider shall ensure that the Wallet Unit generates and securely stores within the WSCD all key material required for PID issuance before initiating a PID issuance request with a PID Provider.

**Requirement** · obligation: **mandatory** · [PDF page 49](pathname:///files/edi-stelsel/2026-11-06/NL-P-04W_Wallet_Onboarding__Lifecycle_Mngt_-_reqs_-_RC1.0_-_for_pub.pdf#page=49)

**How a CAB verifies this:** A CAB verifies this requirement by inspecting the issuance flow and confirming that the binding key material exists in the secure cryptographic device before the issuance request is sent.



### OPS-7.2-02 {#ops-7-2-02}

The Wallet Provider shall ensure that the Wallet Unit presents the Wallet User with a clear description of the PID issuance process and obtains the Wallet User's explicit consent before initiating a PID issuance request with a PID Provider.

**Requirement** · obligation: **mandatory** · [PDF page 49](pathname:///files/edi-stelsel/2026-11-06/NL-P-04W_Wallet_Onboarding__Lifecycle_Mngt_-_reqs_-_RC1.0_-_for_pub.pdf#page=49)

**How a CAB verifies this:** A CAB verifies this requirement by reviewing the documented PID issuance flow and confirming that a description is shown and that issuance does not proceed until the Wallet User has given explicit consent. Where feasible, the CAB may also run the PID issuance flow to confirm the description is shown and consent is required.



## 8.1 PID Issuance request

[Read section 8.1 in the full text](/edi-stelsel-certification/text/nl-p-04w#s-8-1)

### PID-8.1-01 {#pid-8-1-01}

The Wallet Unit shall obtain the registration certificate of a PID Provider exclusively from the credential issuer metadata published by that PID Provider, as profiled in \[5\].

**Requirement** · obligation: **mandatory** · [PDF page 51](pathname:///files/edi-stelsel/2026-11-06/NL-P-04W_Wallet_Onboarding__Lifecycle_Mngt_-_reqs_-_RC1.0_-_for_pub.pdf#page=51)

**How a CAB verifies this:** A CAB verifies this requirement by reviewing the provider verification logic of the Wallet Unit and confirming that no alternative retrieval is attempted when the registration certificate is absent from the credential issuer metadata. Where feasible, the CAB may also present the Wallet Unit with credential issuer metadata from which the registration certificate has been removed and confirm that no alternative retrieval is attempted.



### PID-8.1-02 {#pid-8-1-02}

The Wallet Unit shall verify, prior to submitting a PID issuance request, that the registration certificate and the access certificate of the PID Provider contain the same unique identifier for that PID Provider.

**Requirement** · obligation: **mandatory** · [PDF page 51](pathname:///files/edi-stelsel/2026-11-06/NL-P-04W_Wallet_Onboarding__Lifecycle_Mngt_-_reqs_-_RC1.0_-_for_pub.pdf#page=51)

**How a CAB verifies this:** A CAB verifies this requirement by reviewing the comparison logic and confirming that a mismatched pair of certificates is detected. Where feasible, the CAB may also

**Referenced by:** [PID-8.1-03](/edi-stelsel-certification/requirements/nl-p-04w#pid-8-1-03)

### PID-8.1-03 {#pid-8-1-03}

The Wallet Unit shall not submit a PID issuance request where the verification specified in [PID-8.1-02](/edi-stelsel-certification/requirements/nl-p-04w#pid-8-1-02) does not confirm that both certificates contain the same unique identifier.

**Requirement** · obligation: **mandatory** · [PDF page 52](pathname:///files/edi-stelsel/2026-11-06/NL-P-04W_Wallet_Onboarding__Lifecycle_Mngt_-_reqs_-_RC1.0_-_for_pub.pdf#page=52)

**How a CAB verifies this:** A CAB verifies this requirement by reviewing the issuance logic and confirming that no issuance request is transmitted when a mismatched pair of certificates is present. Where feasible, the CAB may also present the Wallet Unit with a mismatched pair of certificates and confirm, by observing the network traffic, that no issuance request is transmitted.



### PID-8.1-04 {#pid-8-1-04}

The Wallet Unit shall inform the Wallet User where verification of the PID Provider's registration certificate does not confirm that the PID Provider is registered and explain the danger to the Wallet User.

**Requirement** · obligation: **mandatory** · [PDF page 52](pathname:///files/edi-stelsel/2026-11-06/NL-P-04W_Wallet_Onboarding__Lifecycle_Mngt_-_reqs_-_RC1.0_-_for_pub.pdf#page=52)

**How a CAB verifies this:** A CAB verifies this requirement by reviewing the documented handling of a failed registration verification and the message it presents to the Wallet User. Where feasible, the CAB may also trigger a failed registration verification on a test Wallet Unit and inspect the message presented to the Wallet User.



## 8.2 Binding Wallet Unit to Wallet User Identity Verification

[Read section 8.2 in the full text](/edi-stelsel-certification/text/nl-p-04w#s-8-2)

### PID-8.2-01 {#pid-8-2-01}

The Wallet Provider shall ensure that the Wallet Unit accepts PID only after the PID Provider has confirmed, through identity proofing at Level of Assurance High as specified in \[2\], that the Wallet User is the natural person to whom the PID data uniquely and unambiguously corresponds.

**Requirement** · obligation: **mandatory** · [PDF page 52](pathname:///files/edi-stelsel/2026-11-06/NL-P-04W_Wallet_Onboarding__Lifecycle_Mngt_-_reqs_-_RC1.0_-_for_pub.pdf#page=52)



### PID-8.2-02 {#pid-8-2-02}

The Wallet Provider shall ensure that the identity proofing result presented by the PID Provider refers unambiguously to the same Wallet User session and Wallet Unit that initiated the PID issuance request, such that the result of identity proofing performed for one Wallet User cannot be redirected to a different Wallet Unit.

**Requirement** · obligation: **mandatory** · [PDF page 53](pathname:///files/edi-stelsel/2026-11-06/NL-P-04W_Wallet_Onboarding__Lifecycle_Mngt_-_reqs_-_RC1.0_-_for_pub.pdf#page=53)

**How a CAB verifies this:** A CAB verifies this requirement by reviewing the technical design of the PID issuance flow and confirming that a valid identity proofing result cannot be redirected to a different Wallet Unit. Where feasible, the CAB may also attempt, in a test environment, to redirect a valid identity proofing result to a different Wallet Unit and confirm that this fails.



### PID-8.2-03 {#pid-8-2-03}

The Wallet Provider shall implement controls to detect and interrupt PID issuance flows that exhibit patterns inconsistent with legitimate first-time or renewal issuance for a single Wallet Unit, including repeated rapid issuance attempts and concurrent issuance sessions for the same Wallet Unit.

**Requirement** · obligation: **mandatory** · [PDF page 53](pathname:///files/edi-stelsel/2026-11-06/NL-P-04W_Wallet_Onboarding__Lifecycle_Mngt_-_reqs_-_RC1.0_-_for_pub.pdf#page=53)

**How a CAB verifies this:** A CAB verifies this requirement by reviewing the Wallet Provider's documented ratelimiting and anomaly detection policy for PID issuance and confirming that the Wallet Provider has a documented process for responding to detected anomalous issuance patterns. Where feasible, the CAB may also test the issuance flow with rapid repeated attempts on a single Wallet Unit to confirm that the rate limit is enforced and further attempts are interrupted.



### PID-8.2-04 {#pid-8-2-04}

The Wallet Provider shall ensure that PID binding is initiated only upon verified and cryptographically confirmed successful completion of the required identity verification steps, and that any PID issuance session associated with a failed, interrupted, or unverifiable identity verification result is rejected and cancelled prior to PID storage.

**Requirement** · obligation: **mandatory** · [PDF page 54](pathname:///files/edi-stelsel/2026-11-06/NL-P-04W_Wallet_Onboarding__Lifecycle_Mngt_-_reqs_-_RC1.0_-_for_pub.pdf#page=54)

**How a CAB verifies this:** A CAB verifies this requirement by reviewing the PID issuance protocol specification and confirming that the protocol includes a step in which the Wallet Provider validates a session-bound assertion before initiating binding. Where feasible, the CAB may also test the scenario in which the identity verification service returns an error or no response and confirm that no PID credential is bound to the Wallet Unit in this case.



### PID-8.2-05 {#pid-8-2-05}

The Wallet Provider shall ensure that the Wallet Unit does not simultaneously store more than one active PID credential purporting to identify the same natural person, and shall require the Wallet User to remove any existing active PID credential issued by a different PID Provider before a new PID credential from that different PID Provider can be accepted and stored.

**Requirement** · obligation: **mandatory** · [PDF page 55](pathname:///files/edi-stelsel/2026-11-06/NL-P-04W_Wallet_Onboarding__Lifecycle_Mngt_-_reqs_-_RC1.0_-_for_pub.pdf#page=55)

**How a CAB verifies this:** A CAB verifies this requirement by reviewing the documented issuance procedure and status handling and confirming that, when a Wallet Unit already holds an active PID credential, a second PID from a different PID Provider is handled by either (i) prompting the Wallet User to remove the existing PID before the new one can be accepted, or (ii) rejecting the second PID credential if the first is still present, and that the second PID is accepted once the first has been removed. Where feasible, the CAB may also test this scenario on a Wallet Unit that already holds an active PID credential.



## 8.3 Secure PID Reception Process

[Read section 8.3 in the full text](/edi-stelsel-certification/text/nl-p-04w#s-8-3)

### PID-8.3-01 {#pid-8-3-01}

The Wallet Unit shall verify, prior to accepting a PID credential, that the signing certificate of the PID Provider that issued the credential traces to a trust anchor published by the European Commission in the list of trusted entities applicable to PID Providers.

**Requirement** · obligation: **mandatory** · [PDF page 55](pathname:///files/edi-stelsel/2026-11-06/NL-P-04W_Wallet_Onboarding__Lifecycle_Mngt_-_reqs_-_RC1.0_-_for_pub.pdf#page=55)

**How a CAB verifies this:** A CAB verifies this requirement by reviewing the credential validation logic and confirming that a PID credential signed by a key not registered in the trusted list is rejected without being accepted or stored. Where feasible, the CAB may also present such a credential to the Wallet Unit and confirm that it is rejected without being accepted or stored.



### PID-8.3-02 {#pid-8-3-02}

The Wallet Unit shall reject a PID credential whose signing certificate traces to a trust anchor other than a trust anchor published by the European Commission in the list of trusted entities applicable to PID Providers, established in accordance with \[12\].

**Requirement** · obligation: **mandatory** · [PDF page 56](pathname:///files/edi-stelsel/2026-11-06/NL-P-04W_Wallet_Onboarding__Lifecycle_Mngt_-_reqs_-_RC1.0_-_for_pub.pdf#page=56)

**How a CAB verifies this:** A CAB verifies this requirement by reviewing the trust anchor validation logic and confirming that a credential signed under an anchor not sourced from the trusted list is rejected. Where feasible, the CAB may also install an additional trust anchor on a test device, present a credential signed under that anchor, and confirm that the Wallet Unit rejects the credential.



### PID-8.3-03 {#pid-8-3-03}

The Wallet Provider shall ensure that, for each PID issuance, the Wallet Unit generates a dedicated asymmetric key pair (the PID binding key pair) within the Wallet Secure Cryptographic Device (WSCD), and that the PID issuance request submitted to the PID Provider includes a cryptographic proof of possession of the PID binding private key together with a Key Attestation from the Wallet Provider confirming that the PID binding private key is generated, stored within, and non-extractable from the WSCD.

**Requirement** · obligation: **mandatory** · [PDF page 56](pathname:///files/edi-stelsel/2026-11-06/NL-P-04W_Wallet_Onboarding__Lifecycle_Mngt_-_reqs_-_RC1.0_-_for_pub.pdf#page=56)

**How a CAB verifies this:** A CAB verifies this requirement by reviewing the technical specification of the PID issuance flow and confirming the presence of proof of possession and Key Attestation in the issuance request.



### PID-8.3-04 {#pid-8-3-04}

The Wallet Provider shall ensure that the PID Provider binds the issued PID credential to the PID binding public key, such that the credential can only be presented by the Wallet Unit holding the corresponding PID binding private key.

**Requirement** · obligation: **mandatory** · [PDF page 57](pathname:///files/edi-stelsel/2026-11-06/NL-P-04W_Wallet_Onboarding__Lifecycle_Mngt_-_reqs_-_RC1.0_-_for_pub.pdf#page=57)

**How a CAB verifies this:** A CAB verifies this requirement by reviewing the presentation validation logic and confirming that a PID credential cannot be presented from a Wallet Unit that does not hold the PID binding private key corresponding to the public key in the credential.



### PID-8.3-05 {#pid-8-3-05}

The Wallet Provider shall ensure that, upon any PID issuance or re-issuance, the Wallet Unit generates a PID binding key pair that is unique to that issuance event and has not been used as the PID binding key pair for any other PID credential issued to the same Wallet Unit, so that the compromise of one PID binding private key does not affect the security of any other PID credential.

**Requirement** · obligation: **mandatory** · [PDF page 57](pathname:///files/edi-stelsel/2026-11-06/NL-P-04W_Wallet_Onboarding__Lifecycle_Mngt_-_reqs_-_RC1.0_-_for_pub.pdf#page=57)

**How a CAB verifies this:** A CAB verifies this requirement by reviewing the Wallet Provider's technical specification and confirming that it mandates fresh key generation for every PID issuance event. Where feasible, the CAB may also initiate two successive PID issuances for the same Wallet Unit and compare the PID binding public keys included in the respective proof of possession claims, expecting the two public keys to be different.



### PID-8.3-06 {#pid-8-3-06}

The Wallet Unit shall verify the cryptographic integrity and authenticity of a received PID credential before storing it, including verification of the PID Provider's digital signature over the credential, the credential's validity period, and conformance of the credential format with the applicable technical specification.

**Requirement** · obligation: **mandatory** · [PDF page 58](pathname:///files/edi-stelsel/2026-11-06/NL-P-04W_Wallet_Onboarding__Lifecycle_Mngt_-_reqs_-_RC1.0_-_for_pub.pdf#page=58)

**How a CAB verifies this:** A CAB verifies this requirement by reviewing the credential validation logic and confirming that a PID credential with a tampered payload that invalidates the issuer signature is detected and rejected without being stored. Where feasible, the CAB may also present such a tampered credential and confirm that the Wallet Unit detects the invalid signature and rejects the credential without storing it.



### PID-8.3-07 {#pid-8-3-07}

The Wallet Provider shall ensure that the delivery of a PID credential from the PID Provider to the Wallet Unit takes place in conformance with the requirements specified in ETSI TS 119 472-3 \[5\], applying any additional protective measures required to prevent observation, modification, or interception of the credential payload by parties intermediating the communication path.

**Requirement** · obligation: **mandatory** · [PDF page 58](pathname:///files/edi-stelsel/2026-11-06/NL-P-04W_Wallet_Onboarding__Lifecycle_Mngt_-_reqs_-_RC1.0_-_for_pub.pdf#page=58)

**How a CAB verifies this:** A CAB verifies this requirement by reviewing the Wallet Provider's technical documentation to confirm that the PID issuance protocol implemented by the Wallet Instance conforms to the requirements defined for the Wallet in ETSI TS 119 472-3 \[5\]. The CAB verifies that the solution passed the OpenID Foundation self-certification positively. The CAB additionally examines functional test results for the issuance flow, covering the authorisation code flow and, where applicable, the pre-authorised code flow, and confirms correct handling of the WIA, WUA, and access certificate verification steps specified in ETSI TS 119 472-3 \[5\].



### PID-8.3-08 {#pid-8-3-08}

The Wallet Provider shall ensure that, before the Wallet Unit signs the proof of possession that binds a PID credential to the Wallet Unit, the Wallet User has successfully authenticated to the Wallet Unit using the authentication mechanism established during Wallet Unit activation.

**Requirement** · obligation: **mandatory** · [PDF page 59](pathname:///files/edi-stelsel/2026-11-06/NL-P-04W_Wallet_Onboarding__Lifecycle_Mngt_-_reqs_-_RC1.0_-_for_pub.pdf#page=59)

**How a CAB verifies this:** A CAB verifies this requirement by reviewing the issuance flow documentation and confirming that the Wallet Unit signing event for the proof of possession is gated by Wallet User authentication. Where feasible, the CAB may also attempt on a test Wallet Unit to trigger PID binding from a state in which no recent authentication has occurred and confirm that the binding does not proceed without prompting the Wallet User to authenticate.



## 8.4 PID Storage and Protection

[Read section 8.4 in the full text](/edi-stelsel-certification/text/nl-p-04w#s-8-4)

### PID-8.4-01 {#pid-8-4-01}

The Wallet Provider shall ensure that the PID binding private key associated with each issued PID credential is generated within the WSCD of the Wallet Unit, stored exclusively within that WSCD, and protected from extraction in plaintext form throughout the lifecycle of that PID credential.

**Requirement** · obligation: **mandatory** · [PDF page 60](pathname:///files/edi-stelsel/2026-11-06/NL-P-04W_Wallet_Onboarding__Lifecycle_Mngt_-_reqs_-_RC1.0_-_for_pub.pdf#page=60)

**How a CAB verifies this:** A CAB verifies this requirement by reviewing the technical architecture documentation for the Wallet Unit, confirming that PID binding key pairs are generated using the WSCD’s internal key generation functionality, and confirming that the WSCD enforces non-extractability of private key material through its access control and export policy mechanisms.



### PID-8.4-02 {#pid-8-4-02}

The Wallet Provider shall ensure that all personal data stored by the Wallet Instance, including Person Identification Data, Electronic Attestations of Attributes, transaction log entries, and any other personal data of the Wallet User, is encrypted at rest using a cryptographic key whose use is authorized only after successful Wallet User authentication via the authentication mechanism established during Wallet Unit activation.

**Requirement** · obligation: **mandatory** · [PDF page 60](pathname:///files/edi-stelsel/2026-11-06/NL-P-04W_Wallet_Onboarding__Lifecycle_Mngt_-_reqs_-_RC1.0_-_for_pub.pdf#page=60)

**How a CAB verifies this:** A CAB verifies this requirement by reviewing the Wallet Instance's storage layout and the key-derivation or key-release path, confirming that PID credential data on disk is ciphertext and that the path requires Wallet User authentication. Where feasible, the CAB may also inspect the storage in a controlled environment and attempt to read the PID credential from the device's file system without supplying Wallet User authentication, confirming that no readable PID payload is recoverable.



### PID-8.4-03 {#pid-8-4-03}

The Wallet Provider shall ensure that the Wallet Unit requires successful Wallet User authentication before presenting any PID credential to a relying party, using the authentication mechanism established during Wallet Unit activation at the assurance level applicable to the Wallet Unit.

**Requirement** · obligation: **mandatory** · [PDF page 61](pathname:///files/edi-stelsel/2026-11-06/NL-P-04W_Wallet_Onboarding__Lifecycle_Mngt_-_reqs_-_RC1.0_-_for_pub.pdf#page=61)

**How a CAB verifies this:** A CAB verifies this requirement by reviewing the documented presentation flow and confirming that a PID presentation cannot complete without Wallet User authentication on the Wallet Unit and that a session established for device unlock alone does not bypass this gate. Where feasible, the CAB may also attempt to initiate a PID presentation without first completing Wallet User authentication and confirm that the Wallet Unit refuses to complete the presentation.



### PID-8.4-04 {#pid-8-4-04}

The Wallet Provider shall ensure that the Wallet Unit requires successful Wallet User authentication, using the authentication mechanism established during Wallet Unit activation, before rendering any value of a Person Identification Data attribute in its Wallet User interface.

**Requirement** · obligation: **mandatory** · [PDF page 61](pathname:///files/edi-stelsel/2026-11-06/NL-P-04W_Wallet_Onboarding__Lifecycle_Mngt_-_reqs_-_RC1.0_-_for_pub.pdf#page=61)

**How a CAB verifies this:** A CAB verifies this requirement by reviewing the documented PID credential view behaviour and confirming that credential values are not rendered until the Wallet User supplies the wallet authentication factor, even after operating-system unlock without prior wallet authentication. Where feasible, the CAB may also open the Wallet Unit on a test device after operating-system unlock, navigate to the PID credential view, and confirm that the values are not rendered until the wallet authentication factor is supplied.



## 8.5 Wallet User Activation of PID

[Read section 8.5 in the full text](/edi-stelsel-certification/text/nl-p-04w#s-8-5)

### PID-8.5-01 {#pid-8-5-01}
